parts.title: Learning to ride
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I learnt to ride a bike when I was eight, but I was much slower than my friends. My cousin Max could ride without help when he was five, and he liked to remind me of this. It made me determined to improve.

My grandfather offered to teach me in the park on Sunday mornings. He was seventy at the time, and he could not run beside me, so he stood in the middle of the path and cheered. On my first try, I fell into a bush. On my second, I rode five metres before crashing into a bench.

The turning point came on the fourth Sunday. My grandfather told me to stop looking at my feet and look at the end of the path instead. I did what he said, and suddenly the bike seemed to balance itself. I rode right round the pond without stopping, and my grandfather clapped as if I had won a race.

Now I cycle to school every day. Last year, I even overtook Max on a hill. I have never mentioned it to him, but I think he knows.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer want to improve?
options: His school had a big race
His parents were disappointed in him
questions.explanation: Max liked to remind him he rode earlier.

questions.prompt: How did the grandfather help?
options: He encouraged from the middle of the path
He held the back of the seat
He ran beside the bike all the way
questions.explanation: He stood in the middle of the path and cheered.

questions.prompt: What was the secret of success?
options: Pedalling as fast as he possibly could
Looking at the end of the path
Using a smaller bicycle than before
questions.explanation: He stopped looking at his feet and looked at the end of the path.

questions.prompt: How did the grandfather react to the success?
options: He took a photograph of him
He gave him a brand new bike
questions.explanation: He clapped as if the boy had won a race.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about Max now?
options: He once overtook Max on a hill
questions.explanation: Last year he overtook Max on a hill.

parts.title: A cycle to work scheme
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
More and more people in our city are cycling to work, and the council wants to encourage even more. [1] Last year, it spent two million pounds on new cycle lanes that are separated from the traffic, so that cyclists feel much safer than before.

The council has also started a new scheme with local companies. [2] In return, the companies must provide showers and safe places for bikes.

Workers say that the changes are making a difference. [3] One office worker, Anita, says she now saves twenty pounds a week on bus tickets and arrives at work feeling fresher. [4] Not everyone is convinced, though. Some drivers complain that the cycle lanes take space from the roads.

[5] The council promises to keep listening to everybody and says that more changes will follow next year.
sentences: Employees who cycle to work get a small payment for every journey.
It has already made a number of changes to the streets.
The number of cyclists has gone up by a third in two years.
Cycling is also cheaper than going by car or by bus.
The company was started more than fifty years ago.
This debate is likely to continue for some time.

gaps.explanation: The council has already made changes, and the next sentence gives an example.
The scheme gives a payment to employees, and "in return" the companies provide showers.
Cycling numbers rising is what workers say, followed by a personal example.
"Also cheaper" adds to the benefits, before the objection from some drivers.
The debate will continue is a fitting link to the council promising to listen.

parts.title: An email about a bike
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Hi Lucy, Guess what? I [1] a new bicycle for my birthday last week! It is bright red, and it [2] twenty-one gears. I [3] to school on it every day since Monday. It is much faster than my old one, [4] it also makes less noise. Yesterday, I rode for two hours without [5] tired. Would you like to go for a ride [6] me this Saturday? We could go to the lake and have a picnic there, if the weather is nice.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: Past simple: "I got a new bicycle".

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Third person singular: "it has".

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: "Since Monday" needs the present perfect.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: "And" adds information.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: After "without" we use -ing.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: Go for a ride "with" me.

parts.title: Bike safety tips
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Cycling is a great way to travel, but it is important to stay safe on the road, especially in the city. First of all, always wear a helmet, even [1] your journey is short. Make sure your lights work [2] it gets dark, and wear bright clothes so that drivers can see you. Never use your phone [3] you are riding. Always give a clear signal with your hand before you turn. Remember that red traffic lights are for cyclists [4] well as for cars. You should also check your brakes and tyres once [5] week. If you follow these simple rules, [6] will enjoy many safe and happy journeys.

gaps.explanation: Lights should work "when" it gets dark.
Never use your phone "while" you are riding.
We say "once a week", so the article "a" is needed here.

parts.title: A talk about the cycling club
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: peter
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the Riverside Cycling Club. I'm Peter, the club secretary. We meet every Sunday at nine in the morning outside the library. We have three groups. The slow group rides about twenty kilometres, the medium group thirty-five, and the fast group sixty. Everyone must wear a helmet, and we recommend bright jackets. Membership costs thirty pounds a year, which includes insurance. For young people under eighteen, it is only fifteen pounds. After each ride, we usually stop at a café for tea and cake. In July, we organise a weekend trip to the coast, and last year thirty people joined us. If you want to try a ride before you join, you can come for free the first time.

gaps.explanation: Membership costs thirty pounds a year.

gaps.prompt: After each ride, they stop at a ___
gaps.explanation: We usually stop at a café.

gaps.prompt: The July trip is to the ___
gaps.explanation: A weekend trip to the coast.

parts.title: A cyclist
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Today, I'm talking to Marisol Park, who cycled around Europe last summer. Marisol, why did you decide to do that?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: I wanted to see the countries slowly. When you are on a bike, you notice everything: the smells, the sounds and the people.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: How far did you go?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: About four thousand kilometres in nine weeks. Some days I rode a hundred kilometres, but on others I only did thirty.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Where did you sleep?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: A mixture of cheap hostels and campsites. Once I slept in a farmer's barn, which was really comfortable.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Did anything go wrong?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: I had four punctures and one broken chain. In Austria, a kind man helped me to fix the chain, and he refused to take any money.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What was your favourite moment?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Reaching the top of a high mountain in Italy. I was exhausted, but the view was incredible, and the ride down was wonderful.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Would you do it again?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Definitely. Next year I would like to cycle through Asia, but first I need to save some money.

questions.explanation: She wanted to see the countries slowly.

questions.explanation: About four thousand kilometres in nine weeks.
